title: Demonstration
source: Bundled North America example: ERA5 daily maximum temperature, April–September 1996–2025

types.name: Widespread (Isolated)
types.meaning: One regionally extensive day whose heatwave cells form a single cluster, so SCORCH fits one ellipse.

types.name: Spatially Clustered
types.meaning: One regionally extensive day whose heatwave cells form several separate clusters, each with its own ellipse.

types.name: Temporally Clustered
types.meaning: Several consecutive days with the same pattern every day: always one cluster, or always several clusters.

types.name: Compound Clustering (Multi-Type)
types.meaning: Several consecutive days whose pattern changes: one-cluster and several-cluster days are mixed, or a day forms no cluster.

events.reason: 6 consecutive regionally extensive days with a mix of one-cluster and several-cluster days
One regionally extensive day with one cluster
7 consecutive regionally extensive days with one cluster on every day
One regionally extensive day with 3 separate clusters

terms.cell: Heatwave cell: a grid cell inside a local heatwave that day, a run of at least 3 days with at least 3 of them at or above the cell's own 95th percentile of daily maximum temperature.
terms.day: Regionally extensive day: at least 351 of the 1800 cells are heatwave cells, the 97.5th percentile of all analyzed days.
terms.cluster: Cluster: neighbouring heatwave cells grouped by DBSCAN. Cells it leaves out stay grey.
terms.ellipse: Ellipse: the principal axes of a cluster, each 1.25 standard deviations long from the centre, drawn around the temperature-weighted centroid.
terms.event: Compound event: consecutive regionally extensive days. Its type follows the number of clusters on each day.
